# Acme

> Acme keeps projects, milestones and the reasons behind each decision in one shared plan, so a small team always knows what ships next.

## Getting started

Source: https://example.com/help/getting-started/

Learn the basics and make your first changes.

## First steps

Explore the site, read our guides, and start shaping your product story.

1. Review your site settings.
2. Update your home page sections.
3. Share your work with your team.

## Where to go next

- **Create your account** if you have not signed up yet.
- **Invite your team** once you are ready to work together.

## Create your account

Source: https://example.com/help/create-your-account/

Sign up with your work email and set up your workspace.

## Sign up

Choose **Get started** on the home page and enter your work email. We send a link to confirm the address.

## Name your workspace

A workspace holds your projects and your team. Most teams use the company name. You can rename it later in **Settings**.

## Invite your team

Source: https://example.com/help/invite-your-team/

Add teammates to your workspace and choose what each person can do.

## Send invitations

Open **Settings → Members** and choose **Invite**. Enter one or more email addresses, separated by commas.

## Choose a role

- **Admin** — manages billing, members and every project.
- **Member** — creates and edits projects.
- **Guest** — sees only the projects shared with them.

You can change a role at any time.

## Create a project

Source: https://example.com/help/create-a-project/

Start a project from scratch or from a template.

## Start a project

Choose **New project**, give it a name, and pick who can see it. Projects are private to their members until you share them.

## Use a template

Templates come with tasks and milestones already in place. Pick one that matches your work and adjust it as you go.

## Organise work with milestones

Source: https://example.com/help/organise-work-with-milestones/

Group tasks under a shared goal and date to track progress.

## Add a milestone

In a project, choose **New milestone**, then set a name and a target date.

## Track progress

Each milestone shows how many of its tasks are done. It turns amber when the date is near and work is still open.

## Share a project

Source: https://example.com/help/share-a-project/

Give clients or teammates outside the project a link to follow along.

## Share with a link

Open the project, choose **Share**, and turn on **Anyone with the link can view**. Copy the link and send it.

## Stop sharing

Turn the link off at any time. Anyone who had it loses access straight away.

## Choose a plan

Source: https://example.com/help/choose-a-plan/

Compare plans and change yours whenever your team grows.

## Compare plans

Every plan includes unlimited projects. Paid plans add more members, guests, and priority support. See the **pricing section** on the home page.

## Change your plan

Admins can upgrade or downgrade in **Settings → Billing**. Changes take effect immediately and are prorated.

## Reset your password

Source: https://example.com/help/reset-your-password/

Get back into your account when you cannot sign in.

## Request a reset link

On the sign-in page, choose **Forgot password** and enter your email. The link is valid for one hour.

## Still locked out?

Check your spam folder, then contact support from the address you signed up with.

## How we run design reviews

Source: https://example.com/blog/how-we-run-design-reviews/

Thirty minutes, one decision, and written feedback before anyone joins the call.

## Feedback comes first, in writing

The designer shares the work a day ahead. Reviewers leave written comments before the meeting, so the call is for decisions, not first impressions.

## One decision per review

Every review ends with a single outcome: ship it, change it, or try another direction. If we cannot decide, we name who will and by when.

## Keep it short

Thirty minutes is enough. Long reviews tend to drift into redesigning the whole product.

## Release notes people actually read

Source: https://example.com/blog/release-notes-people-read/

Lead with the change a customer will notice, keep it short, and show a picture.

## Start with the outcome

"You can now export reports as PDF" beats "We added a new export pipeline". Readers want to know what they can do, not how you built it.

## One change per paragraph

Short paragraphs are easy to skim. If a change needs more than three sentences, link to a help article instead.

## Show it

A single screenshot or short clip answers most questions before they are asked.

## How to plan a launch in one week

Source: https://example.com/blog/plan-a-launch-in-a-week/

A day-by-day plan for small teams that need to ship something real by Friday.

## Monday: decide what "done" means

Write one sentence that describes the launch from the customer's side. Everything that does not serve that sentence moves to next week.

## Tuesday and Wednesday: build the smallest version

Split the work into tasks no bigger than half a day. If a task feels bigger, it is two tasks.

## Thursday: rehearse

Walk through the launch as a customer would: the page, the sign-up, the first email. Fix what trips you up.

## Friday: ship and tell people

Publish, then write a short note about what changed and why. A launch nobody hears about is only a deploy.

## Introducing milestones

Source: https://example.com/blog/introducing-milestones/

Group related tasks under one goal, see progress at a glance, and know what ships next.

## Why milestones

Projects rarely fail on a single task. They slip when nobody can see how the pieces add up. Milestones give a set of tasks one shared goal and one date, so the whole team can see how close you are.

## How they work

1. Open a project and choose **New milestone**.
2. Give it a name and a target date.
3. Drag tasks onto it, or pick the milestone when you create a task.

Each milestone shows a progress bar based on completed tasks, and turns amber when the date is close and work is still open.

## Available today

Milestones are available on every plan. Read **Organise work with milestones** in the help center for the details.

Source: https://example.com/blog/welcome/

News, ideas, and updates from the Acme team.

## Welcome

We're glad you're here. Follow along for product updates, practical tips, and stories from our team.

## What to expect

We post a few times a month, in three categories:

- **Product** — new features and the thinking behind them.
- **Guides** — step-by-step advice you can use today.
- **Company** — how we work and who we are.
